title: Decision Leverage
hook: I spent a week picking a logo and ten minutes deciding my pricing. Completely backwards.
statement: A handful of decisions drive most of your results. Give those the most weight and the most time.
explainer: Not every decision deserves the same energy. Agonize over the small stuff and you rush the big stuff. Sort them by impact, not by how loud they are.
sop: List every decision in front of you this month.
Rate each one's Weight and Outcome from 1 to 10.
Rank them by Impact, not by urgency.
Give the top few real time: research, advice, sleep on it.
Decide the small ones fast and move on.
equation_example: Weight 9 × Outcome 8 = 72. That one deserves real thinking time. Higher means slow down and deliberate. Lower means decide fast and move on.
question: Write down the biggest decision in front of you and how much time you've actually given it.
closing_statement: Give your biggest decisions the time they deserve.
caption:
Principle Nº 183: Decision Leverage

I spent a week picking a logo and ten minutes deciding my pricing. Completely backwards.

A handful of decisions drive most of your results. Give those the most weight and the most time.

Your turn: Write down the biggest decision in front of you and how much time you've actually given it.
